req.purpose: Load a stored parameter set into the running machine.
content: Scrollable list of the format files present on the machine, one row per format.
Per row: format name, and the metadata needed to tell two similar formats apart (suggested: date of last change, author or access level that saved it).
The format currently loaded is marked in the list.
Empty state when no format is stored yet.
interaction: Tapping a row selects it (single selection, no immediate effect).
A primary action button loads the selected format.
Loading overwrites live machine settings, so it must be confirmed in a dialog that names the format and warns that unsaved changes are lost.
While the machine is running, loading has to be blocked or the machine stopped first - decide which.
req.access: Read from L1; loading a format from L2 (to be confirmed).
req.data: File system, not the parameter list. The format file contains a snapshot of the parameter values.
open: Where are formats stored - internal memory, USB, or both?
What exactly does a format contain: every parameter, or a defined subset (without network and user settings)?
Is loading allowed while running?

req.purpose: Overwrite an existing format with the current settings.
content: Same list component as Select Format, but the action is "overwrite", not "load".
Per row: format name plus date of last change, so the user sees what they are about to replace.
The currently loaded format is marked and should be the default selection.
interaction: Selecting a row and confirming overwrites that file with the current live values.
Confirmation dialog naming the target file - this action destroys data.
Optional but recommended: a short diff ("12 parameters differ") before confirming, which replaces the Compare/Check screen that was dropped from the diagram.
req.data: File system; reads the live parameter values at the moment of saving.
open: Is the dropped Compare/Check function meant to come back as this diff, or is it gone for good?
May a format be renamed here, or only overwritten?

req.purpose: Store the current settings as a new format file.
content: One text input field for the format name, pre-filled with a proposal (suggested: device name + date).
Alphabetical keyboard, unfolding below the field.
Visible rule text for what a valid name is (length, allowed characters).
interaction: Save is disabled until the name is valid and not already in use.
Duplicate name: either block with an inline message or offer "overwrite instead".
After saving, return to Formats with a confirmation toast.
req.data: File system; writes a snapshot of the live parameter values.
open: Maximum name length and allowed character set?
Is there an upper limit for the number of stored formats?

req.purpose: Verify the external encoder and show the resulting production rate.
content: Live value of the measured external encoder, in m/min and in Hz, updating continuously.
Button to run the speed test.
Result block: time needed for the next label dispensed / cycle, and the rated pieces per minute (product rate).
Timestamp or "live" marker so the user knows whether the value is current.
interaction: The live fields update while the screen is open; leaving the screen stops the measurement.
No encoder signal: show "no signal" rather than 0.
The test itself may move the machine - say so before it starts.
req.access: Read from L1, running the test from L2 (to be confirmed).
req.data: Info_Speed_Test_Measured, Info_Product_rate and Button_Speed_Test from the parameter list; the live values come from the drive, not from a stored parameter.
open: Update rate of the live values?
Info_Product_rate has no Type in the parameter list - Float with what unit, pieces/min?
Does the product rate depend on Calc_Product_Rate_Enable being on?

req.purpose: See the state of every digital IO and, at L3, force outputs for commissioning.
content: Table of all digital IOs of the MIO card and the other IO groups.
Columns: pin name, direction (in/out), assigned function, live state.
State shown as a clear on/off indicator, not just text - it is read at a glance while probing hardware.
Grouping or a filter by IO group, since the list is long.
interaction: Live update of the input states while the screen is open.
With L3 access, outputs can be forced; a forced output must be visibly marked and must reset when the screen is left or after a timeout.
Forcing outputs can move the machine: an explicit warning and an "all outputs back to normal" action are required.
req.access: Read from L1; forcing outputs L3 only.
req.data: Live IO states from the firmware. Pin assignment comes from the MIO configuration, not from a parameter.
open: How many IOs in total, and how are they grouped?
Does a forced output survive leaving the screen? Recommended: no, with an automatic timeout.
Is forcing logged in the audit trail? (CRA-relevant)

req.purpose: Switch diagnosis recording on and review what the machine recorded since.
content: Toggle bar at the top of the screen that activates diagnosis recording.
Chronological list of internal events since activation: user logins, parameter changes (old value to new value), state changes, errors.
Per entry: timestamp, event type, user role, detail text.
Visible indication of how long recording has been on and how much space is left.
interaction: Switching the toggle off keeps the recorded list until it is cleared.
The list is scrollable and should be filterable by event type.
Export to USB is expected - confirm.
req.access: L2 to view, L3 to activate and to clear (to be confirmed).
req.data: Log file written by the firmware. The activation state replaces the separate "Button/Switch Activate Diagnosis" screen of the previous diagram - it currently has no parameter in the list.
open: Activation needs its own parameter so the state survives a restart.
Ring buffer or fixed size, and what happens when it is full?
Is the diagnosis log the same thing as the audit trail, or a second, separate log? Two logs with overlapping content are a maintenance trap.

req.purpose: Find out what went wrong, when, and who was logged in at the time.
content: Scrollable list of error messages, newest first.
Per entry: error ID, message text, severity, timestamp, and the user role logged in at that moment.
Search field that unfolds an alphabetical keyboard.
Empty state and an end-of-list marker.
interaction: Search filters while typing, over ID and message text.
A row can be opened for the full text if the message is longer than the row.
Sorting is fixed to newest first; a filter by severity is recommended.
req.access: Read from L1 (an operator has to be able to report an error); clearing L3 only, if clearing is allowed at all.
open: Retention: how many entries, how long, and what happens on overflow? (CRA-relevant)
Is the audit trail allowed to be cleared? For CRA purposes it should not be, or only with an entry documenting the clearing.
Export format for a service report - CSV, PDF, or the QR route?

req.purpose: Close out a service visit: document what was done and reset the service counters.
content: Read-only block with the counters since the last service (distance, time, labels - the same values as on Information/Counters).
Multi-line text field for the technician comment.
Date and the logged-in user are added automatically and shown.
interaction: Commit writes a text entry into the log and resets the "since last service" counters.
Because the reset is irreversible, it needs a confirmation dialog that states which counters are reset.
Empty comment: allow but warn, or block - to be decided.
req.access: L2 or L3 (service), to be confirmed.
req.data: Counters from the parameter list (read); the comment goes into the log file, not into a parameter.
open: Which counters exactly are reset - only the four "since last service" ones, or also the error counters?
Is the entry exportable, and does it belong in the audit trail?

req.purpose: Write a backup to a USB drive, or load one back into the machine.
content: File browser over the USB drive: path bar, folder rows, file rows, one level up.
Files that are not machine backups are greyed out or filtered.
Action button "Create backup here" for the folder currently open.
Follow-up dialog: editable file name, pre-filled with device name + serial + date, and a choice between "Backup" (everything) and "Format" (parameter set only).
interaction: No USB drive: the screen shows an empty state, not an error dialog.
Loading a backup is a machine-changing action - confirmation dialog, and the machine must not be running.
Long operations need a progress state and a result message; the user must not be able to pull the drive without a warning.
req.access: L3 for load, L2 for create (to be confirmed).
req.data: USB file system. The backup content is defined by firmware, not by the parameter list.
open: What is in a "Backup" as opposed to a "Format" - network settings, users, logs?
Are backups signed or checksummed, and what happens on a broken file? (CRA-relevant)
Is loading a backup from a different machine type allowed?

req.purpose: Select a firmware file from a USB drive and install it.
content: Same file browser component as Load/Store Backup, filtered to firmware files.
Current firmware version and the version of the selected file, side by side.
Clear statement of what happens during the update (machine stops, reboot).
interaction: Install is a single, clearly separated primary action with a confirmation step.
Progress display with a phase text; no back navigation during the update.
Result screen with success or failure and the resulting version.
open: Signature check and rollback behaviour on a failed update (CRA-relevant).
Is a downgrade allowed?
Does the update keep parameter values, and what happens to parameters that the new version does not know?

req.purpose: Hand machine context to a service form on the phone without typing it.
content: Generated QR code, large enough to be scanned from about 30 cm.
Below it, in plain text, what the code contains and what happens when it is scanned.
The machine data that goes into the link, visible so the user knows what is being shared.
interaction: The code is built from a URL plus machine-specific information (serial number and more) and pre-fills a web form.
The code must be regenerated when the underlying data changes.
Marked in the diagram as planned for later - show it as a preview screen, not as a finished function.
req.data: URL template plus machine identification. The template has to be configurable and does not exist in the parameter list yet.
open: Which fields go into the link, and is any of it personal data?
Where does the URL template come from - fixed in firmware, or a parameter?
What does the screen show when the machine has no serial number set?

req.purpose: Reach a parameter directly instead of walking the menu tree.
content: Search field with an unfolding alphabetical keyboard and a numeric mode for IDs.
Result rows: parameter name, its menu path, and its current value.
Empty state before typing, "no match" state after.
interaction: Search runs over parameter ID and name; from two characters onwards.
Selecting a result opens the screen that contains the parameter, with the row highlighted - not a detached editor.
Back returns to the result list, not to the menu root.
req.access: Results should be filtered by access level: a parameter the user may not read is not listed.
req.data: Parameter list. Needs a search index, including the translated names.
open: Is the search over the English names only, or over the translated labels too?
Should recently used parameters be offered before typing?

req.purpose: Create a user account and store it in the secure user database.
content: Input fields: Name, Password, Access Level, Auto LogOff (Time), Language.
Password field masked, with a visibility toggle and live feedback against the rules from User Settings (length, capitals, symbols, numbers).
Access Level as a selection limited to the levels the creator may hand out.
Language as a selection - a new user should see their own language at first login.
interaction: Save is only enabled when every rule is met; violations are shown per field, not as one dialog at the end.
Duplicate user name is rejected inline.
After saving, the account appears in User Management.
Cancel must warn about losing the entry.
req.access: L3 minimum to create L1/L2/L3 accounts. An L3 user must not be able to create a higher level than their own.
req.data: Secure user database (firmware side), not the parameter list. The password rules come from User Settings (ParamID 618-627).
open: Is the password stored as a hash? It has to be, for CRA - please state it in the spec.
What is the maximum number of users?
Is there a forced password change at first login (User_PW_Change_first_login = True) and what does that flow look like?
The diagram mentions black-listed and white-listed parameters per user - is that configured here or in User Management?

req.purpose: Self-service for the logged-in user, and user administration for higher levels.
content: The screen has two faces, decided by the level of the logged-in user.
L1/L2: change own password, change language temporarily (value set back afterwards), disable own role.
L3: list of enabled users with name, role and date of last password change.
L3 per user: password, access level, auto log-off time, language, black-listed parameters, white-listed parameters, disable user.
interaction: One screen, two layouts - the frontend needs both states drawn, plus the transition when the level changes mid-session.
"Disable own role" logs the user out; it needs a confirmation that says so.
"Temporary language change" has to state when it is set back - on logout, or after the standby timer.
The black-/white-list needs a parameter picker, which is a screen of its own and is not yet drawn anywhere.
req.access: L1/L2 see only their own account. L3 sees the list and may edit levels 1-3. Level 0 (not logged in) has no access to this screen at all.
req.data: Secure user database. Nothing here is in the parameter list.
open: There is an L4 in this description while the rest of the system uses three levels - is L4 a real level, or is it L3 = super admin?
What exactly does the parameter black-/white-list do, and how does an admin pick from 330 parameters on a 4.3" screen?
Does temporary language survive a restart? (It should not.)
Is deleting a user allowed, or only disabling? For an audit trail, disabling is the safer answer.

req.purpose: Controlled, time-limited service access beyond the normal levels.
content: QR code generated by the machine from a URL plus machine-specific data (serial number and more) that pre-fills a request form.
Plain-text explanation of what the code is for and what happens next.
Field for entering the code that comes back, with a numeric or alphanumeric keyboard.
State display: whether an elevated access is currently open and until when.
interaction: Entering a valid code opens the elevated access for a defined time and then closes it again by itself.
Every opening and closing must appear in the audit trail.
The backlog also lists a "button for data erase" - that is a destructive action and needs its own confirmation flow, not a button next to the others.
req.access: Visible from L3. The access it grants is level 4 (Secure Access) and is bound to the code and its time window, not to a user profile.
req.data: URL template, machine identification, and a code check in the firmware. Backlog entries: "Parameters for Secure Code", "Parameters for hiding port of database, ports, SSH etc. (high level access) - self resetting".
open: This is a documented back door: the spec needs who may request it, how long it stays open, what it unlocks, and what is logged. (CRA-relevant)
Is the code bound to one machine and one time window?
What does "self resetting" mean exactly - after a time, after a reboot, or both?
Does "data erase" wipe user data, logs, or the whole parameter set?
